notes.meaning: Temple leaders and the captain of the guard suddenly approached Peter and John while they were teaching. These Jewish leaders watched over the temple grounds and wanted to stop the commotion. God used this moment so the apostles could share the good news with the highest council in the nation.

The religious leaders were deeply annoyed and angry. The Sadducees did not believe that anyone rises from the dead, yet the apostles were teaching that Jesus had risen. This message proved the Sadducees wrong and showed that God had vindicated Jesus.

The temple guards seized Peter and John and locked them up. It was late in the afternoon, and Jewish legal practice did not allow trials to take place at night. They held the two men in custody until the council could meet the next morning.

Even though the preachers were put in prison, God's message could not be stopped. Many people who heard their words believed in Jesus, bringing the number of men to about five thousand. Persecution against the church only helped the truth spread further.

The next morning, the Jewish high council known as the Sanhedrin assembled in Jerusalem. This powerful court included the ruling elders, teachers of the law, and high priests like Annas and Caiaphas. Influential men from the high priest's family gathered to judge the two apostles.

The council brought Peter and John out and placed them in the center of the semicircle. They questioned the apostles about whose authority or power they had used to heal the lame man. They hoped to intimidate the disciples or catch them claiming unlawful magical powers.

Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit at that exact moment to answer the court. The Spirit gave him great courage to speak clearly before the nation's rulers. This fulfilled Jesus' promise to give his followers the right words when put on trial.

Peter pointed out that they were being examined for doing something good. Healing a crippled beggar was an act of mercy and help, not a crime. His answer showed how unfair it was for the court to treat a good deed like an offense.

Peter proclaimed that the man was healed by the authority of Jesus Christ from Nazareth. He directly told the rulers that while they had crucified Jesus, God had raised him from the dead. The healed man standing right beside them was living proof of the risen Lord's power.

Peter quoted Psalm 118 to show that Scripture foretold what took place. The religious leaders were like builders who tossed aside a stone they thought was useless. God took that rejected stone, Jesus, and made him the primary cornerstone of his spiritual house.

Salvation, which means rescue from sin and eternal judgment, can be found in no one else. God has given no other name in the entire world by which people must be saved. Peter moved from the healing of a sick body to the eternal salvation that comes only through Jesus.

The council members were amazed at how boldly Peter and John spoke. They realized the apostles were ordinary working men who had never attended the formal rabbinic schools. Yet they recognized that these men had spent time with Jesus and learned from him.

The healed man stood right beside the apostles for everyone in the court to see. Because his lifelong lameness was well known, nobody could deny that a genuine miracle had taken place. The rulers were left completely speechless and had no argument against them.

The rulers sent the apostles out of the room so they could confer in private. They admitted among themselves that a notable miracle had taken place and they could not deny it. To protect their own authority, they decided to threaten the apostles so the message about Jesus would spread no further.

The council called Peter and John back inside and gave them a strict order. They commanded them never to speak or teach in the name of Jesus again. The leaders hoped that strong threats would silence the good news for good.

Peter and John replied that God's authority is higher than any human court. They told the rulers to judge for themselves whether it was right to obey people rather than God. Because they had personally seen and heard the risen Lord, they could not keep quiet.

The council threatened the apostles again and then let them go. The leaders could find no way to punish them because all the people were glorifying God for the miracle. The man who had been healed was over forty years old, making the work of God undeniable.

As soon as they were released, Peter and John returned to the other believers. They shared everything the chief priests and elders had commanded and threatened. Instead of scattering in fear, the church gathered together to face the danger as one family.

The believers responded by praying out loud together in one accord. They addressed God as the Sovereign Lord who created heaven, earth, sea, and everything in them. Remembering his absolute control over creation gave them peace in the face of human threats.

The believers quoted Psalm 2, which was spoken by the Holy Spirit through King David. The psalm predicted that kings and nations would rise up and plot against God and his Messiah, his anointed King. The church recognized that this ancient prophecy was coming to pass in their own day.

The prayer pointed out how the prophecy was fulfilled in Jerusalem. King Herod and Pontius Pilate had joined forces with Roman soldiers and Jewish leaders against Jesus. Both Jews and Gentiles united in rebellion against God's holy Servant.

Even while those rulers attacked Jesus, they were only carrying out what God had already determined would happen. God used their evil choices to accomplish his plan of salvation on the cross. The wicked men remained responsible for their deeds, yet God remained in complete control.

differ.view: God eternally planned and determined everything that took place, directing even wicked acts to accomplish his holy purpose.
God permitted evil rulers to crucify Jesus according to his plan of salvation, without causing or willing their sinful choices.

notes.meaning: The believers did not ask God to destroy their enemies or remove all danger. Instead, they asked the Lord to pay attention to the threats and grant courage to his servants. They prayed for bold hearts so they would keep preaching God's word faithfully.

They asked God to stretch out his powerful hand to heal diseases and afflictions. They wanted miraculous signs to happen through the name of Jesus to confirm their preaching. These wonders would show that the risen Christ was actively working through his followers.

When the believers finished praying, the meeting place was shaken as a physical sign of God's presence. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began preaching the word of God with great boldness. God answered their request right away by giving them supernatural courage.

differ.view: Believers who had already received the baptism in the Holy Spirit were filled again with fresh power to face persecution.
Believers are baptized into the Spirit once when saved, but they experience ongoing fillings of the Spirit for bold service.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The shaking was a visible sign of God's presence that stirred the believers' hearts with a fresh outpouring of divine grace.

notes.meaning: The large group of believers was united in heart and mind. They loved one another so deeply that nobody treated personal belongings as private property. Instead, they shared whatever they owned freely with anyone who had a need.

differ.view: True Christian love naturally led the early believers to share all their goods in common as long as that unity lasted.
Believers shared their property voluntarily and kept personal ownership, without setting up a system of common ownership.

notes.meaning: The apostles continued to preach with powerful evidence that the Lord Jesus had risen from the dead. This resurrection was the central truth of their message. God's rich grace and favor rested abundantly on the whole community of believers.

No one in the community went without help because property owners sold houses and land to provide for others. They brought the money and placed it at the apostles' feet as an act of trust. The apostles then gave out the funds to make sure every needy person was cared for.

Joseph, a Levite from the island of Cyprus, was named Barnabas by the apostles, which means Son of Encouragement. He owned a field, sold it, and brought all the money to the apostles' feet to aid the poor. His generous gift served as a clear example of Christian love in action.
